This suggests that Forodesine may act through a mechanism that is broadly applicable to T-cell malignancies, potentially through shared pathways or targets. The presence of Romidepsin as a downstream target in multiple pathways supports the hypothesis that Forodesine may exert its effects via a mechanism that involves microtubule inhibition or other pathways that are relevant to T-cell biology. The integration of these pathways highlights the potential for Forodesine to be a candidate for repurposing in this specific lymphoma type, provided further mechanistic validation is conducted.
